solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: African took part in race, carrying baton

indicators.note: carrying means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: someone who took part in a race ran
a baton, like a conductor's, is a wand

explanation.surface: A runner from Africa competing in a relay with the baton in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Rwanda, a central African country, is an African.

clue.text: Snake in the grass half-heartedly made sound between a hiss and a rattle

definitions.text: made sound between a hiss and a rattle

indicators.note: in means the snake sits inside the trimmed grass
half the heart of the word is lost: of its two middle letters, one goes

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A treacherous snake in the grass makes a feeble, half-hearted hissing rattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake in the grass' reads as a traitor, the idiom, but here it splits into a snake and the grass it hides in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasp is a harsh grating noise, somewhere between a hiss and a rattle.

clue.text: Old primates OK fitness class being introduced

indicators.note: being introduced means the class is put inside the word for agreement

parts.note: amen expresses assent, much like OK
PE is physical education, a school fitness class

explanation.surface: Elderly primates approve of a new exercise class being brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ape-like early hominids are popularly called by this term, prehistoric primates.

clue.text: Was Spice Girl performing half-cut on noisy tube?

parts.note: read as the question 'Did Geri do?', 'Was ... performing' becomes did ... do
Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice in the Spice Girls
to perform a piece is to do it

indicators.note: half-cut keeps only the first half of the little word on

explanation.surface: Was a pop singer drunk ('half-cut') while performing on some loud wind instrument?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' looks like British slang for drunk but trims ON to O. The Spice Girls were a 1990s British pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aboriginal Australian wind instrument is a long wooden tube giving a loud droning sound.

clue.text: Nearly time when The Sun sinks into obscurity

definitions.text: when The Sun sinks into obscurity

parts.note: nigh means nearly, as in 'nigh on'

explanation.surface: It is almost the moment when The Sun newspaper fades into irrelevance.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised 'The Sun' suggests the tabloid; it is just the sun setting into darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: After sunset the sky turns dark, the hours of darkness that follow dusk.

clue.text: Obtain favourable treatment

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a cure is a medical treatment

explanation.surface: Get yourself preferential medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: To get hold of or acquire something is a synonym of obtaining it.

clue.text: Unable to pay debts, first write your half off

indicators.note: first says the writing and trimmed word go before the debts

parts.note: to pen something is to write it

indicators.note: half off takes away the front half of the word your, keeping its back half

parts.note: IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Advice to someone insolvent: first write off half of what you owe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unable to pay debts' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'pay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone extremely poor and destitute cannot pay what they owe.

clue.text: Love London-based bank that produces notes

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
BoE is the Bank of England, in the City of London

explanation.surface: Affection for the central bank that issues banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bank of England does print banknotes, so 'notes' looks like money; here they are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument makes musical notes.

clue.text: Knock dinner up to try to prevent collapse

indicators.note: to knock up something is to make it hastily, so these letters are thrown together anew

explanation.surface: Rustle up a meal to stop someone fainting from hunger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock dinner up' looks like making a quick meal; Knock rearranges DINNER and UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To support from below, shoring up a structure so it does not fall.

clue.text: Complicated gears pull all but the end organ stops?

indicators.note: complicated means these letters are tangled into a new order
all but the end drops the final letter of pull

explanation.surface: Intricate gears pull all the organ stops except the last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ stops' are levers on a church organ; here the organ is the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Plugs worn in the ears block, or stop up, the hearing organ.

clue.text: Savings at first returning low rate

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of savings
returning means the word for low is read backwards

parts.note: a deep voice is a low one

explanation.surface: Savings are initially earning a poor interest rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Velocity, the pace of travel, is a rate.

clue.text: Prisoner kept in by the authority of succeeding head of government — this could blow up

indicators.note: succeeding means the next part follows that letter
head of takes the first letter of government
kept in means the prisoner is held inside the other word

parts.note: under someone's authority is under them
POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: A prisoner held under the rule of the next government chief might explode.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunpowder Plot of 1605 aimed to blow up Parliament, fitting the political surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosive powder that can blow things sky-high.

clue.text: Attempt to master alphabet's beginning with first three letters in a row — like ABC?

indicators.note: first puts those spelt letters ahead of the rest

parts.note: L, M and N are consecutive in the alphabet; spelt as names they are el, em, en

indicators.note: to master is to hold, so the attempt contains the letter

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: beginning takes the opening letter of alphabet's

explanation.surface: A child trying to learn the alphabet starting from its first three letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First three letters' suggests ABC, but means L, M, N written out as words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as simple as ABC is basic and rudimentary.

clue.text: I'll leave bar, being put on 'nil by mouth'

indicators.note: being put on means the trimmed bar sits alongside, after, the nil

parts.note: nil is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: I'll leave says the letter I will be removed from the bar

parts.note: a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: A patient told 'nil by mouth' must leave the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nil by mouth' is a hospital instruction meaning a patient may not eat or drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken orally means swallowed, administered through the lips.

clue.text: Country expert perhaps involved in upcoming event Simon organised

indicators.note: upcoming says the hidden letters are read backwards
involved in says the letters lie concealed within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rural specialist may be part of an upcoming event that Simon has arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'involved' in the definition; 'involved in' is the indicator for the concealed letters, so the definition ends at 'perhaps'. In a down clue 'upcoming' reads the letters bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A soil and crop scientist is one example of a specialist in countryside matters.

clue.text: Take care of gram plant found around wetland — very unexpected

indicators.note: found around means the gram and plant sit near the wetland, following it

parts.note: to mind something is to take care of it
a bog is wet marshy land
ling is heather, a moorland plant

explanation.surface: A gardener tending a tiny plant in a marsh gets a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so astonishing it boggles the mind, wholly surprising.

clue.text: Perfect pairing Emma rated going awry

indicators.note: going awry means these letters go wrong, out of their order

explanation.surface: Emma rated a supposedly ideal couple who then went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pairing' must be read loosely: the answer is an ideal combination of people, not literally two.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal combination of partners or players, the best possible side.

clue.text: I can be yours for a herbal tea?

definitions.text: I can be yours for a herbal tea?

parts.words: I can be yours for a herbal tea?
parts.note: a herbal tea speaks, offering itself to whoever lifts the cup, and is a restorative drink

explanation.surface: An offer of companionship in exchange for a cup of herbal tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The tea talks: 'choose me, lift me' is its plea, and a tonic drink is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic or refreshing drink taken to revive someone is this kind of thing.

clue.text: Emphasise old resistance is source of tension

parts.note: to stress a word is to emphasise it
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Insisting that old opposition causes strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that causes strain or anxiety in a person is one.

clue.text: Prelude 'variation on a theme' being withdrawn

parts.note: an intro is a prelude
a version is a variant form of something

explanation.surface: A musical introduction offering variations on a theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being shy and inward-looking, the opposite of extroversion.

clue.text: Section of Manhattan Mahler composed

indicators.note: composed suggests the composer, but means these letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A part of a New York concert that the composer Mahler wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of northern Manhattan in New York City.

clue.text: Agitated, as alternative is leaving bully in charge

indicators.note: is leaving says the alternative word is taken out of the bully

parts.note: to hector is to bully
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone flustered when an alternative candidate walks away and leaves the tyrant running things.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic, frenzied, rushed and feverish.

clue.text: Observe with sly glance on turning

indicators.note: on turning means the sly glance word is read backwards

parts.note: a peek is a quick furtive look

explanation.surface: Watching with a furtive look while turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe a rule or custom is to honour or maintain it.

clue.text: American priest to make speech better

parts.note: Eli is the biblical priest who taught Samuel
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: A US clergyman preparing to deliver an improving sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve something, make it better, is to do this; here 'better' is a verb.

clue.text: Authorised escape

definitions.meaning: informal for lawful or genuine, above board
read as two words, ... is slang for run away

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for lawful; split in two it is slang for running off.

clue.text: Go over European river that's rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the river is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Oder flows between Germany and Poland

explanation.surface: Crossing a continental river whose water level is climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something again, repeating or revising it.

clue.text: Tag geese wandering around river — you won't find one laying this!

definitions.text: you won't find one laying this!

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the river
wandering means these letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: Ringing wandering geese near a river; none of them will lay this sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is a goose: no bird lays a chocolate one.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate treat given at the spring festival, not laid by any bird.

clue.text: Small detached piece of land won't be available for rent

definitions.meaning: already rented, so not on the market

explanation.definitionFit: A tiny island; split as two words it says a property is already leased.

clue.text: A document creating act

parts.note: a, as in 'once a day', means per
a form is an official document to fill in

explanation.surface: A piece of paperwork that establishes a legal act.
explanation.definitionFit: To act a part on stage is to play it.

clue.text: Carry equipment of DJ, say, having godlike status

parts.note: to tote is to carry
a disc jockey uses a mic, a microphone

explanation.surface: Hauling around a DJ's gear, as if it were a sacred idol.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a revered emblem or spirit, an object treated as sacred.
